knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=2 x - y^{2} z$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨2 u v,\,- u,\,2 u - 2 v^{2}⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate while holding the other parameter fixed:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨2 v,\,-1,\,2⟩\\\mathbf r_v&=⟨2 u,\,0,\,- 4 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Form the cross product, including the negative middle cofactor:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\2 v&-1&2\\2 u&0&- 4 v\end{vmatrix}=⟨4 v,\,4 u + 8 v^{2},\,2 u⟩.
$$

Take its nonnegative magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{\left(4 v\right)^{2}+\left(4 u + 8 v^{2}\right)^{2}+\left(2 u\right)^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{20 u^{2} + 64 u v^{2} + 64 v^{4} + 16 v^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the coordinates into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 \left(2 u v\right) - \left(- u\right)^{2} \left(2 u - 2 v^{2}\right)\\&=- 2 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 u v.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor. The missing expression is

$$
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{20 u^{2} + 64 u v^{2} + 64 v^{4} + 16 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \left(20 u^{2} + 64 u v^{2} + 64 v^{4} + 16 v^{2}\right)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{20 u^{2} + 64 u v^{2} + 64 v^{4} + 16 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 2 u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{20 u^{2} + 64 u v^{2} + 64 v^{4} + 16 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 2 u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{24 u^{2} + 64 u v^{2} + 64 v^{4} + 16 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{24 u^{2} + 64 u v^{2} + 64 v^{4} + 16 v^{2}}\end{aligned}

knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=x + 2 y^{2} z$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u v,\,- u,\,2 u - v^{2}⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate while holding the other parameter fixed:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨v,\,-1,\,2⟩\\\mathbf r_v&=⟨u,\,0,\,- 2 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Form the cross product, including the negative middle cofactor:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\v&-1&2\\u&0&- 2 v\end{vmatrix}=⟨2 v,\,2 u + 2 v^{2},\,u⟩.
$$

Take its nonnegative magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{\left(2 v\right)^{2}+\left(2 u + 2 v^{2}\right)^{2}+\left(u\right)^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 4 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the coordinates into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=\left(u v\right) + 2 \left(- u\right)^{2} \left(2 u - v^{2}\right)\\&=4 u^{3} - 2 u^{2} v^{2} + u v.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor. The missing expression is

$$
\begin{aligned}&\left(4 u^{3} - 2 u^{2} v^{2} + u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 4 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{aligned}&\left(4 u^{3} - 2 u^{2} v^{2} + u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \left(5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 4 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}\right)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(4 u^{3} - 2 u^{2} v^{2} + u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 4 v^{4}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(4 u^{3} - 2 u^{2} v^{2} + u\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 4 v^{4}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(4 u^{3} - 2 u^{2} v^{2} + u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 4 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(4 u^{3} - 2 u^{2} v^{2} + u\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 4 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}\end{aligned}

knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=- x - 2 y^{2} z$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u v,\,- 2 u,\,u - 2 v^{2}⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate while holding the other parameter fixed:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨v,\,-2,\,1⟩\\\mathbf r_v&=⟨u,\,0,\,- 4 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Form the cross product, including the negative middle cofactor:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\v&-2&1\\u&0&- 4 v\end{vmatrix}=⟨8 v,\,u + 4 v^{2},\,2 u⟩.
$$

Take its nonnegative magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{\left(8 v\right)^{2}+\left(u + 4 v^{2}\right)^{2}+\left(2 u\right)^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 64 v^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the coordinates into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=- \left(u v\right) - 2 \left(- 2 u\right)^{2} \left(u - 2 v^{2}\right)\\&=- 8 u^{3} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} - u v.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor. The missing expression is

$$
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 8 u^{3} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} - u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 64 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{aligned}&\left(16 u^{3} - 32 u^{2} v^{2} - u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 64 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 8 u^{3} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} - u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{6 u^{2} + 16 u v^{2} + 32 v^{4} + 64 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 8 u^{3} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} - u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \sqrt{5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 64 v^{2}}\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(- 8 u^{3} + 16 u^{2} v^{2} - u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \left(5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 64 v^{2}\right)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&\left(16 u^{3} - 32 u^{2} v^{2} - u v\right)\\&\quad\cdot \left(5 u^{2} + 8 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 64 v^{2}\right)\end{aligned}
